title.title: Assignment: Your Contract, Live
title.subtitle: The hands-on finale. Design the contract for your own problem, send a real transaction on a testnet, then explore contracts that hold real money.

brief.heading: Your smart contract, live on a testnet
brief.subtitle: Take your Assignment 1 problem one step further: design its contract, then send a real transaction. No coding needed.

partA.title: Design your contract
partA.lead: In plain language, the contract at the heart of a solution to your Assignment 1 problem:

rows.label: What it holds
rows.desc: The information it stores on-chain: its [state](kw:state).

rows.label: Who can call what
rows.desc: Open to anyone, or restricted? That is [access control](kw:access).

rows.label: What it can't do
rows.desc: One real limit: no outside data without an [oracle](kw:oracle), it can't trigger itself, its rules are hard to change ([immutability](kw:immutability)).

partA.note: "A database would do most of this" is a fine conclusion: say why.

partB.title: Send a real transaction
partB.lead: The wizard on the next slide guides every step. Test funds only, no real money.
submit: 2–3 sentences on what you did and what changed on-chain
partB.note: Covers the syllabus requirement: a testnet transaction to a smart contract.
partB.cta: Do it now: open the wizard

bonus.title: Make it your own
bonus.lead: Deploy your own minimal contract for your Assignment 1 problem, and send your transaction to that one.
bonus.ai: Prompting an AI is fine: Remix's AI or any coding agent.
bonus.explain: You don't need to be a programmer. You need to explain what you shipped.
bonus.cta: Warm up on a live contract

labels.design: Part A: a sensible design for your problem
labels.tx: Part B: a valid transaction, with proof

rules: One PDF on Moodle: Part A, your Part B proof, and the bonus if you did it.
AI is allowed and encouraged. Say in one line how you used it, and be ready to explain every step.
Testnet only: never real funds, and never paste a recovery phrase anywhere.

explore.heading: Explore a real contract
explore.subtitle: Ask the four Part A questions of contracts that hold real money. Then poke a tiny one on the testnet.

usdc.look: A proxy: Code opens the logic contract. Find blacklist and pause. Who is allowed to call them?

weth.look: Short, with no owner and no admin. Find deposit and withdraw. Who could change these rules?

dai.look: Find mint, then the word auth next to it. Which addresses does that let through?

explore.questionsLabel: Talk it through: the Part A questions

questions.label: State
questions.desc: What does it remember? Find where the balances live.

questions.label: Functions
questions.desc: Which actions does it offer? Which only read, and which change state and cost gas?

questions.label: Access
questions.desc: Which functions can anyone call, and which need a special role?

questions.label: Limits
questions.desc: Who, if anyone, can still change the rules after deployment?

poke.label: Poke · anyone can write to this one
poke.what: a greeting and a counter, in under 30 lines
steps: Read Contract: note greeting and counter.
Write Contract: press Connect to Web3 (wallet on Sepolia), type a greeting into setGreeting, confirm.
Read again: the greeting is yours and counter went up by one. Until someone overwrites it.
poke.warning: Public and permanent: write nothing personal. This contract is not ours, and anyone can overwrite the greeting.
poke.bonus: deploy your own copy, then reshape it for your Assignment 1 problem.

keyPoints.s8-first-tx: A transaction is a signed request to change shared state. Once it is included in a block, it is public and it stays.
keyPoints.s8-explore: Verified source means you don't have to take a contract's word for it: read the code, then check the state yourself.
